summary: The article surveys recent innovations to make networks resilient against internet outages, which increasingly harm business, healthcare, and education. It covers causes of outages, AI-based prediction, tougher physical cables, redundancy, mesh networks, satellite fallback, legislation, and community programs. It concludes that a concerted effort is underway to make outages rare.
one_line: Overview of technological, policy, and community innovations, from AI monitoring to mesh and satellite networks, aimed at preventing and quickly recovering from internet outages.
key_facts: On October 14, 2023, New York suffered a significant outage that impacted thousands of businesses during peak hours.
On November 23, 2023, London's internet users saw a massive connectivity dip due to a fiber cut caused by construction activities.
Dr. Jane Holloway, a tech analyst, said on December 5, 2023: "The internet is the backbone of modern society."
Most outages result from physical damage to cables, malicious cyber activities, or natural disasters; rarely a technical glitch, plus network congestion and overloads.
On September 19, 2023, ISP NetFuture announced AI-based monitoring systems across its network; CTO Mark Richardson said the system learns from historical outages and current performance.
On February 8, 2024, FlexiNet unveiled FlexiShield cables claiming triple the resilience of standard fibers against physical damage.
The Redundant Array of Independent Networks (RAIN) project, spearheaded by Dr. Emily Stewart on March 12, 2024, aims to build a framework for ISPs to integrate redundancy into existing systems.
As reported on January 15, 2024, Boulder, Colorado, began creating a citywide mesh network and saw a dramatic increase in internet resilience.
On April 21, 2024, SpaceX announced successful deployment of its latest satellite constellation, promising improved redundancy for ground networks.
SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Project Kuiper are racing to provide satellite internet as a fallback when terrestrial networks fail.
The Secure and Resilient Networks Act, passed on September 29, 2023, gives ISPs tax breaks and grants to adopt the latest resilience standards.
On November 1, 2023, the city of Asheville launched the 'Connected Community Program', working with local ISPs on tailored crisis response plans.
